title: Count ten tablets out of a stock bottle on a pill counting tray
instruction: Count out exactly 10 tablets from the stock bottle into the counting tray's trough, using the spatula, and close the trough's lid. Leave every other tablet in the stock bottle or on the tray's counting floor, and screw the bottle's cap back on. Never touch a tablet with a gripper or let one fall onto the counter.
context: Pharmacy technicians and pharmacists (about 470,000 and 330,000 US jobs) count tablets by hand on a counting tray many times a day. They open the stock bottle, pour some tablets onto the tray and slide them into the tray's trough a few at a time with a spatula until the count is reached, then close the trough's lid and recap the stock bottle. Afterwards the counted tablets go from the trough's spout into the prescription vial. No tablet is touched by hand, and the count must be exact. This task is the count, from opening the bottle to closing the lid and recapping.
setup:
A pharmacy dispensing counter (the station table) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. Behind the counter's back edge stands a white steel pharmacy shelving unit (two 36 in sections, 12 in deep, 84 in tall) full of stock bottles (fixed, out of reach). On the counter:
(1) A 100-count stock bottle of tablets: a white HDPE round packer, 150 cc, 53.3 mm across and 93.0 mm tall to the top of its 38-400 neck (31 mm bore), 17 g, with a white and blue label; 16 tablets left in it. It stands 17 cm forward and 5 cm left, closed by
(2) its plain (not child-resistant) white PP 38-400 screw cap, 40.5 mm across and 15 mm tall, 4 g: one turn of thread at 6 per inch (4.2 mm per turn); it takes 1.0 N m to break loose and 0.3 N m to keep turning.
(3) The tablets: round, flat-faced film-coated tablets, 10 mm across and 4 mm thick, 0.35 g each, all alike.
(4) A right-handed pill counting tray, light-blue plastic, 21.2 x 14.9 cm and 3.8 cm tall, 100 g, its middle 25.5 cm forward and 6.5 cm right: a flat counting floor 1.95 cm up, inside 1.85 cm walls at the left and back and a 6 mm lip at the front. Down its right side runs a trough (a half-tube 32 mm across inside, its rim level with the floor, with a 2.5 mm rib along the floor's edge) under a blue hinged lid (a half-tube, 12 g) that stands open at 110 degrees. The trough narrows at its far end into a spout 2.5 cm long and 1.8 cm wide. At the near-left corner the floor runs on into a return spout 3 cm long, narrowing to 2.2 cm. A 1 cm spatula slot runs along the outside of its left wall.
(5) In the slot, standing on its edge, a stainless-steel counting spatula: a 127 mm blade, 19 mm wide and 0.8 mm thick, with a round tip, on a 100 mm wooden handle 19 x 11 mm, 30 g; the handle points toward the robot.
The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged on where every tablet is. In the bottle: its centre inside the bottle. In the trough: inside the tray's trough or its spout. On the counting floor: over the tray's floor or its return spout. Down: outside the bottle and the tray, its centre at most 1.2 cm over the counter. Touched: a finger pad pushing a tablet with more than 0.05 N. 0.0 for the whole trial (latched, never reset) if a tablet is ever down or ever touched. Otherwise, at the end, if the bottle was opened (its cap unscrewed off), exactly 10 tablets are in the trough and every other tablet is in the bottle or on the counting floor: 1.0 with the trough's lid shut (within 8 degrees of closed) and the bottle's cap screwed back down (turned at least 300 degrees after its thread caught, within 0.6 mm of its seat); 0.5 with the lid shut; 0.25 with the lid open. Else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit or once the full score has held 1 s with everything still. In a real trial: after the run, open the lid and count the tablets in the trough, and count those in the bottle and on the counting floor (16 in all); the photo and the three videos must show no tablet on the counter or the floor and none pushed by a finger; the cap is screwed down when it stops turning with its skirt at the neck's ledge.
reset_notes: Put all 16 tablets back in the stock bottle and screw its cap down. Stand the bottle and the tray where they were, open the trough's lid fully (it rests at 110 degrees) and stand the spatula in its slot with the handle toward the robot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control), real sizes and masses. Stand-ins: the cap's thread is a joint (4.2 mm per turn; 1.0 N m to break loose, then 0.3 N m; set back on the neck within 6 mm and turned 20 degrees, it catches). Hidden linings stop fast tablets passing through thin walls: the bottle's bore collides 45 mm wide (real about 51 mm), its floor 3 mm and the tray's 10 mm thicker. Tablets are flat discs (friction 0.25). Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
